rendered:
I read your question as asking about the capacity of cobalt-free batteries, including the three NFA variants[1] (cobalt-free cathodes). If you meant something else, let me know.

**The NFA variants (adma-2020).** They all have discharge capacities of about 200 mAh g^− 1 at C/20 between 3 and 4.5 V[2]. Their first-cycle discharge capacities are:
- NFA 811[3]: ≈205[4] mAh/g
- NFA-F: 199[5] mAh/g
- NFA-A: 192 mAh g^− 1[6]

The authors say these capacities are comparable to those of the cobalt-containing NCM and NCA cathodes made the same way. They also report about ≈80% capacity retention[7] after 100 charge/discharge cycles[8].

**Other cobalt-free cathodes (review, aenm-2022).**
- The NMM, NMT and NMA cathodes all deliver capacities of >200 mAh g^− 1[9] when charged to a high cut-off voltage, and offer reasonable capacity retentions >80% after[10] 100 cycles[11].
- Lithium nickel oxide (LNO) has a theoretical capacity ≈ 275 mAh g^− 1[12].
- Disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes reach capacities up to[13] 400 mAh g^− 1[14].
